purpose: Rimantadine is used to help prevent or treat influenza A, which is a type of the flu. It works best when started early — ideally within the first day or two of feeling sick. It can also be given to people who have been exposed to the flu to help prevent them from getting it.
how_it_works: Rimantadine works by blocking the flu virus from getting inside your body's cells. Think of it like putting a lock on the door so the virus cannot enter and multiply. By stopping the virus from spreading inside your body, it helps shorten how long you feel sick and reduces the severity of your symptoms.
common_side_effects: Some people experience nausea, stomach upset, or loss of appetite. You might also notice dizziness, headache, trouble sleeping, or feeling unusually tired or nervous. These effects are usually mild and tend to go away on their own.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you are allergic to rimantadine or similar drugs like amantadine. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, epilepsy, or a history of seizures, as the dose may need to be adjusted. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before taking this medicine. Note that rimantadine does NOT work against influenza B or COVID-19 — only influenza A.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual dose is 100 mg taken twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening). Older adults or people with kidney or liver problems may be given a lower dose of 100 mg once daily. For children, the dose is based on body weight and is usually given once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
